title: Objection Handling
sub: Not comebacks — a repeatable structure you can run on any objection, even one you've never heard.

title: Six steps, every time
displayText: Run the structure, not a memorized line.
note: 1 Acknowledge · 2 Identify what they protect · 3 Clarify the workflow · 4 State our narrow role · 5 Ask a diagnostic question · 6 Continue or disqualify honestly.

title: “We already have intake software.”
obj: We already use Clio Grow / our own intake system.
mean: I don't want another disconnected system to manage.
say: one3seven doesn't replace your intake or case system — it organizes the worker's underlying record before your team has to reconstruct it, then feeds what you already use.
ask: What does your team still assemble by hand before an attorney can screen a matter?

title: “We already use AI.”
obj: We've already got AI in our stack.
mean: We've seen the hype; we're skeptical of one more AI tool.
say: We use AI too — the difference is what we let it do: it organizes and links to the source, and it never judges the case.
ask: Which part of intake does your current AI actually touch — drafting, or the worker's raw record?

title: “Workers won't upload everything.”
obj: Clients won't do the work of uploading documents.
mean: I don't want staff time wasted on half-empty files.
say: The worker owns the record and is motivated — it's their claim — and the system shows them exactly what's missing and writes the request letter for them.
ask: What share of your intakes arrive complete on the first pass today?

title: “Our staff already handles this.”
say: This hands your staff the reconstructed file so they spend their time on judgment, not assembly.
ask: How many hours a week does that assembly take across the team right now?

title: “We don't have enough volume.”
obj: We're not high-volume enough for this.
mean: I'm not sure the value justifies the cost.
say: The value is per-intake time saved and cleaner screening, not raw volume — and if you're genuinely not a fit yet, I'll tell you.
ask: How many potential matters do you turn away or leave half-built each month?

title: “We can't trust AI with legal intake.”
obj: I can't put AI between us and a client file.
mean: My bar license and AB 316 liability are on the line.
say: That's exactly why every fact links to its source page — nothing is taken on faith, everything is one click to verify.
ask: What would it take for you to trust an automated file? (It's almost always traceability.)

sources.label: CA AB 316 — attorney cannot delegate accountability to AI

title: “We don't want another tool.”
mean: I'm tired of onboarding software that doesn't stick.
say: one3seven sits before or beside what you already use — the worker does the work, and your firm simply receives a finished file.
ask: What happens today between a worker first reaching out and an attorney being able to decide?

title: “How is this different from a chatbot?”
obj: Isn't this just a chatbot / document summarizer?
mean: Show me why this isn't a commodity.
say: A chatbot answers questions and a summarizer condenses documents — one3seven builds the worker's own source-linked record and hands them ownership of it. Different job, earlier in the timeline.
ask: Do your current tools produce anything the worker actually keeps and controls?

title: “Can it tell us if they have a case?”
obj: Does it tell us whether the worker has a viable claim?
mean: I want a shortcut to case selection.
say: Our AI identifies the strong cases before your team touches them.
note: This is the objection most likely to tempt a rep across the doctrine line. The correct answer is below — hold it with confidence.

title: The line you hold
say: one3seven organizes and reflects. Your firm makes every legal and screening decision. We show what's present and missing against what the law requires — we never conclude whether there's a claim.
ask: Would a complete, source-linked record make your own screening decision faster?

title: Describe the record. Let the attorney decide.
sub: None of these were comebacks — each acknowledged, clarified the workflow, stated our narrow role, and ended in a question. Run the structure.
